title: KV 4-bit onboarding + evals — weekly notes
body:
Purpose: capture the week’s progress on onboarding a 4-bit quantized variant for customer-facing models, summarize quick evals, list anomalous behaviors when using KV cache, and decide next engineering actions. This doc is intended for the narrow group running experiments and the platform team who will integrate any rollout safety gates.

Attendees: Priya (owner), Diego, Hannah, Samir, Marta; async notes from Jin and Alex.

High-level summary:
- We moved a candidate LLM (open-checkpoint-v3-small) through a lightweight onboarding pipeline using int4 symmetric quantization with our new per-block scaling patch. The model compiles and serves on a single A10G instance.
- Initial evals show a 2.8x token-throughput improvement vs baseline fp16 with negligible downstream QA score regression on our conversational eval set (delta -0.6% on Exact Match).
- Two repeatable anomalous patterns surfaced tied to KV cache + incremental decoding under long context: (1) token collapse after repeated attention to rare tokens when cache hits exceed ~1.2k keys, (2) occasional off-by-one termination when microbatching is used with sequence packing.

Experiments run this week (short notes + key metrics):
- EXP-ML-234-int4-perblock: int4 symmetric per-block scaling, no activation clipping. Results: throughput +2.8x, latency p95 +1.05x (slight increase), EM -0.6%. Memory footprint reduced ~60%.
- EXP-ML-241-kvprefetch: enable early KV prefetch on first 32 tokens for streaming sessions. Results: reduced streaming startup latency by ~45ms, but increased incidence of token collapse in EXP-ML-234 from 0.7% -> 3.4%.
- EXP-ML-247-microbatch-pack: 4-way microbatching with sequence packing to improve GPU utilization. Results: throughput up by 13% vs single request batching at same tail latency SLO; observed off-by-one termination in 1.1% of runs for int4 variant only.

Observed anomalies (details & quick triage):
1) Token collapse with long KV hits (>1200 keys)
   - Symptoms: repeated identical token or short repeated phrase emitted for >10 tokens, usually after the model references a rare entity.
   - Hypothesis: quantization-induced reduced dynamic range in attention scores combined with stale KV scaling accumulates rounding error; top-k softmax becomes overly peaky.
   - Repro steps: run EXP-ML-234 with an injected synthetic dialog where entity tokens are repeated at positions 300, 600, 900; observe output. Repro rate 85% in our env.
   - Temporary mitigations tested: (a) increase softmax temperature by 1.05 only after cache length >800 (reduced collapse to 0.9%), (b) fall back to fp16 for sequences that will exceed 1200 keys (eliminates collapse but loses throughput gains).

2) Off-by-one termination when using sequence packing + microbatching
   - Symptoms: generation ends one token early for certain packed inputs that have uneven end-of-seq alignments.
   - Hypothesis: small bug in packed-offset handling in runtime when using compressed kv indices with int4 layout; index rounding interacts poorly with our end-token detection routine.
   - Quick check: running same packed workload on fp16 variant => no issue. Running same packed workload with int4 but without compressed-kv-index => no issue. Points to compressed index codepath.

Decisions made this week:
- Pause automatic rollout of the int4 variant for sessions that may exceed 1000 cached keys until we ship the KV-safety patch.
- Add a lightweight runtime guard: if cached-keys > threshold, enable softmax-stabilizer (temperature tweak) and signal telemetry event EXP-KV-WARN.
- Prioritize a small change in compressed-kv-index to add bounds-check + unit tests for packing offsets. Low-risk PR assigned.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Diego: prototype a numerically stable attention normalization for int4 attention scores; aim for a POC by 2027-06-18. (JIRA-ML-4879)
- Hannah: create a microbench harness that simulates 1500-key long dialogues across 10k run samples; finish infra by 2027-06-16. (JIRA-ML-4882)
- Samir: author PR for compressed-kv-index bounds-check and add unit tests for packing offsets; aim to land by 2027-06-15. (PR #2137 linked above)
- Marta: extend eval suite with targeted “rare-entity” prompts and track token collapse metric as a first-class CI check; ETA 2027-06-20.
- Priya: update model onboarding checklist and safety gating doc to include "KV cache long-session flag" and softmax-stabilizer option; draft by 2027-06-14. (CONFLUENCE-ML-KV4B-PLAYBOOK)

Risk & mitigation note:
- Risk: early adoption of int4 causes customer-visible regressions only for long-session workloads (support teams may surface these). Mitigation: conservative rollout (version pinning + automatic fallback for flagged sessions), plus feature flag gated telemetry so we can flip back quickly.

Open questions for next sync:
- How do we set a production-safe threshold for fallback vs stabilization? Tradeoffs: throughput loss vs quality risk. Need ops input on customer session distributions.
- Is compressed-kv-index change sufficient or do we need a path that avoids compressed indices for int4 entirely for long sessions? (costly)
- Does temperature tweak introduce artifacts in other eval slices (e.g., knowledge retrieval tasks)? We need cross-slice checks.

Quick experiments to run next week (prioritized):
1) Sweep softmax temperature between 1.0 and 1.2 for sequences crossing 800/1200/1600 keys and measure collapse metric, EM, and perplexity on retrieval set.
2) Run the microbench harness (Hannah) with and without compressed-kv-index to measure throughput hit vs reliability for 4-bit models.
3) End-to-end A/B with dedicated fallback: route 5% of long sessions to int4-stabilizer, 95% to fp16 fallback; log user-visible regression rates.

Notes for product/solutions:
- If a customer requests the int4 variant for cost reasons, we should proactively ask about typical session lengths and recommend dedicated capacity with conservative kv thresholds.
- For Dedicated customers we can ship an "int4-safe long-session" profile that disables compressed-kv-index and accepts smaller throughput gains.

Appendix: quick logs/commands used this week (for reproducibility):
- run_eval.sh --exp EXP-ML-234 --seed 42 --streaming true --kv-threshold 1200
- microbench-run --scenario long-dialogue --runs 10000 --model open-checkpoint-v3-small-int4 --packed true
- docker-compose -f local-serve.yml up --build (to reproduce compressed-kv-index behavior locally)

If you want a TL;DR to drop into Slack: "This week: int4 candidate shows strong throughput wins but two reliability patterns tied to KV-cache and packing emerged. Short-term mitigations in place; patch for compressed-kv-index + numeric stabilization are highest priority next week."

End of notes.
